data.topic: 课上要点 · Class notes (interpretation, not verbatim)

items.zh: 总览 · What this session was about
items.en: Warm-up and extension tied to Lesson 12 (shopping / clothes, 我想买…): textbook-style Mandarin (where things are, towel vs scarf, measure words and radicals) plus real-life wardrobe vocabulary—layers of clothing, “outer” vs “inner,” and colloquial garment terms that rarely appear in chapter 12 alone. Summary below sticks to Chinese-learning threads only.

items.zh: 重复主题 · “Where is it?”（说明）
items.en: Locating things inside other things: 围巾 in 外套, using 里边 / 里面 / 在……里面. Pattern: 在 + container + 里面 = “inside …”

items.py: Wǒ de wéijīn zài wàitào lǐbian.
items.en: My scarf is inside the coat. (的 possession; 在 + place + 里边)
The scarf is inside the clothing. (里面 ≈ 里边 in many contexts)

items.zh: 重复主题 · 毛巾 vs 小毛巾（说明）
items.en: 毛巾 = towel (often larger: bath / hand). For a small face cloth people often say 洗脸巾. 浴巾 = bath towel (after shower / beach). One English word “towel” maps to several Chinese words—pick by size and use.

items.py: Qǐng gěi wǒ yī tiáo máojīn.
items.en: Please give me a towel. (请; 给 + person + object; 条)

items.zh: 洗脸以后用洗脸巾擦一擦。
items.py: Xǐliǎn yǐhòu yòng xǐliǎnjīn cā yi cā.
items.en: After washing your face, use a face cloth to dab. (以后; 用 + tool; 擦一擦 reduplication = “wipe a bit”)

items.zh: 重复主题 · 外套 = generic “outer layer”（说明）
items.en: 外套 = any outer layer you put on over indoor clothes before going out—not only “jacket” in English. Narrow with 夹克、帽衫、羽绒服等. Hypernym vs specific type (like “dog” vs “poodle”).
Before going out you should put on a coat. (出门; 以前; 要 + verb; 穿 + garment)
This coat is very warm. (暖和 for clothing / weather comfort)

items.zh: 重复主题 · 内衣 / 睡衣 / 家居服（说明）
items.en: These words name layers and situations, not one English word “underwear.” 内衣 often means women’s bras (also 文胸); 内裤 is underpants for anyone. 睡衣 is sleepwear; 家居服 is relaxed clothes at home (not necessarily the same as 睡衣). 外衣 is “outer garment” in a broad sense; 外套 is the usual word for a coat/jacket layer. Wrong pairing (wrong register or body part) sounds odd—learn whole phrases, not isolated glosses.

items.py: Wǒ huí jiā jiù huàn shuìyī.
items.en: As soon as I get home I change into pyjamas. (就 = then / right away; 换 = change into)
Before bed you need to change into pyjamas. (以前 = before; 要 = should / need to)

items.zh: 夏天在家我喜欢穿家居服。
items.py: Xiàtiān zài jiā wǒ xǐhuan chuān jiājūfú.
items.en: In summer at home I like wearing loungewear. (在 + place; 喜欢 + verb phrase 穿…)

items.zh: 这件是内衣，那件是外套。
items.py: Zhè jiàn shì nèiyī, nà jiàn shì wàitào.
items.en: This one is underwear, that one is a coat. (这件 / 那件 + 是 … 对比 inner vs outer)

items.zh: 内裤和内衣不一样，别用混了。
items.py: Nèikù hé nèiyī bù yīyàng, bié yòng hùn le.
items.en: Underpants and (other) underwear are not the same—don’t mix them up. (不一样; 别 + verb; 用混了 = use them in a mixed-up way)
Same frame as the textbook title 我想买毛衣: 想 + verb of intent, 买 + object. Swap the object to drill clothes vocabulary.

items.py: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yī jiàn máoyī.
items.en: I want to buy a sweater. (textbook line; 件 for upper-body garments / “matters”)

items.py: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yī tiáo niúzǎikù.
items.en: I want to buy a pair of jeans. (条 for long things: pants, rivers, etc.)

items.zh: 重复主题 · 衣旁 & 体恤（说明）
items.en: Many clothing characters use the form ⻂ (衣字旁): it hints “something worn.” 裙、裤、衬、袜 are built that way. 体恤 / T恤 is different: it is a phonetic loan—English “T” replaces part of the sound—so you do not look for a semantic radical the same way. Compare: 裙 “skirt” shows 衣旁 + 君; T恤 is mainly sound-matching.

items.py: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yī jiàn T xù.
items.en: I want to buy a T-shirt. (体恤／T恤; 一件 + 体恤)

items.py: Zhè jiàn T xù duōshao qián?
items.en: How much is this T-shirt? (same shopping pattern as lesson 11: 这件 … 多少钱)
This skirt is very pretty. (裙子 + 衣旁 on 裙)

items.py: Nà tiáo kùzi tài cháng le.
items.en: Those trousers are too long. (裤子; 太 + adj + 了)

items.py: Tā chuān le yī jiàn bái chènshān.
items.en: He put on a white shirt. (穿 + 了 = completed change; 衬衫 with 巾)

items.zh: 衣字旁的字常常跟穿的衣服有关。
items.py: Yīzìpáng de zì chángcháng gēn chuān de yīfu yǒuguān.
items.en: Characters with the clothing radical often relate to clothes you wear. (…的字; 跟…有关)

items.zh: 重复主题 · 羽绒服（说明）
items.en: 羽绒 = down (feather filling); 羽绒服 = down jacket / puffer. Often used where European learners would say “winter jacket” without specifying filling.

items.zh: 冬天出门我喜欢穿羽绒服。
items.py: Dōngtiān chūmén wǒ xǐhuan chuān yǔróngfú.
items.en: In winter when I go out I like wearing a down jacket. (冬天; 出门; 喜欢 + 穿)

items.zh: 这件羽绒服又轻又暖和。
items.py: Zhè jiàn yǔróngfú yòu qīng yòu nuǎnhuo.
items.en: This down jacket is light and warm at the same time. (又…又… parallel qualities)
Session ended on learner confusion between sounds (e.g. 一万 and similar syllables in fast speech). Worth a short targeted listen-and-repeat, not more vocabulary in that moment.

items.zh: ──────── 后半堂 · Part 2（词语与句型）
items.en: Second half opened with listening to Lesson 12 words (听第十二课的词语) and a quick 一到十 run-through, then: register for 小姐 vs 服务员, long/short clothes and 袖子, measure words (件、顶、双), 太…了 vs …极了, 穿 vs 戴, 你想… chains, 怎么样, 下课以后, 一分钱一分货. Side chat (shops abroad, gender in other languages, silly food jokes) omitted.

items.zh: 重复主题 · 小姐 & 服务员（说明）
items.en: In Lesson 12, 小姐 often means “Miss” (shop assistant). In many real restaurants Mainland Chinese prefer 服务员 (“server”)—clearer and neutral. Context matters: 小姐 alone can sound odd or dated depending on region and tone.
Waiter / waitress, please come here a moment. (safe address in dining)

items.zh: 在餐厅里可以叫“服务员”。
items.en: In a restaurant you can call “server.” (在 + place + 里; 可以 + verb)

items.zh: 重复主题 · 长 / 短 / 袖子（说明）
items.en: 长 cháng = long; 短 duǎn = short. 短裤 / 长裤; 短袖 / 长袖 (袖子 xiēzi = sleeve). Pattern: 穿 + garment; 不要 / 不可以 + 穿 for advice.

items.zh: 今天很冷，穿长袖吧，不要穿短袖。
items.py: Jīntiān hěn lěng, chuān chángxiù ba, bú yào chuān duǎnxiù.
items.en: It’s cold today—wear long sleeves, don’t wear short sleeves. (吧 softens advice; 不要)
In summer he likes wearing shorts. (喜欢 + 穿 + object)

items.zh: 重复主题 · 太…了 vs …极了（说明）
items.en: 太 + adjective + 了 = “too …” (often excessive). …极了 = “extremely …” (strong but not always “too much”). 好极了 = great; 漂亮极了 = stunning; 贵极了 = extremely expensive. Not the same slot as 极乐 (Buddhist bliss)—listen for 极了.

items.py: Zhè jiàn máoyī tài piàoliang le!
items.en: This sweater is so beautiful! (太 + adj + 了 — can be praise or “too much” by context)

items.zh: 这家日本餐厅的寿司贵极了。
items.py: Zhè jiā Rìběn cāntīng de shòusī guì jí le.
items.en: This Japanese restaurant’s sushi is extremely expensive. (…极了; 的 links restaurant to sushi)
Wonderful! (极了 after positive adjective)

items.zh: 重复主题 · 件 / 顶 / 双（说明）
items.en: 件 jiàn: many upper-body garments (一件毛衣、一件外套). 顶 dǐng: hats (一顶帽子). Informally some people say 一个帽子; textbook style prefers 顶. 双 shuāng: natural pairs—一双手套、一双袜子.

items.py: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yī dǐng màozi.
items.en: I want to buy a hat. (顶 for hats)

items.py: Qǐng gěi wǒ yī shuāng wàzi.
items.en: Please give me a pair of socks. (双 = pair; same for 手套)

items.zh: 重复主题 · 穿 vs 戴（说明）
items.en: 穿 chuān: put on / wear clothes on the body. 戴 dài: wear on head, face, wrist, neck—帽子、眼镜、手表、耳环、项链.

items.py: Tā dài zhe màozi, chuān zhe dàyī.
items.en: He’s wearing a hat (on) and wearing an overcoat. (戴着 / 穿着 ongoing state)

items.zh: 我戴眼镜，不戴隐形眼镜。
items.py: Wǒ dài yǎnjìng, bú dài yǐnxíng yǎnjìng.
items.en: I wear glasses, not contact lenses. (眼镜 “glasses,” not 眼睛 “eyes”)

items.zh: 重复主题 · 你想…（说明）
items.en: Chain questions from class: 你想 + verb phrase (买什么 / 吃什么 / 喝什么 / 去哪儿 / 做什么). Answer with 我想… Same pattern as textbook shopping, applied to plans and preferences.
What clothes do you want to buy?
I want to buy long trousers. (contrast 短裤)

items.py: Nǐ xiǎng mǎi duǎnkù háishi chángkù?
items.en: Do you want to buy shorts or long pants? (还是 alternative question)

items.py: Nǐ xiǎng hē shénme? Wǒ xiǎng hē chá.
items.en: What do you want to drink? I want to drink tea.
Where do you want to go travelling?

items.py: Xià kè yǐhòu nǐ xiǎng zuò shénme?
items.en: After class what do you want to do? (下课以后 = after class)

items.zh: 重复主题 · 怎么样（说明）
items.en: 怎么样 asks “how about …?” for suggestions or evaluation. 这家餐厅怎么样？下课以后我们去吃寿司，怎么样？Another use: 你最近怎么样？= “How have you been lately?”

items.zh: 下课以后我们去吃寿司，怎么样？
items.py: Xià kè yǐhòu wǒmen qù chī shòusī, zěnmeyàng?
items.en: After class let’s go eat sushi—how about it? (我们 + 去 + verb; 怎么样 at end)

items.zh: 这家餐厅的寿司怎么样？
items.py: Zhè jiā cāntīng de shòusī zěnmeyàng?
items.en: How is the sushi at this restaurant?

items.py: Yī fēn qián yī fēn huò.
items.en: You get what you pay for. (proverb: price matches quality)

items.zh: 又好又便宜的东西不多。
items.py: Yòu hǎo yòu piányi de dōngxi bù duō.
items.en: Things that are both good and cheap are rare. (又…又…)

items.py: Wǒ xǐhuan hē shuǐ, duì shēntǐ hǎo.
items.en: I like drinking water; it’s good for the body. (对 + noun + 好)
